issues.legal_issue: Whether an appeal concerning a purchaser’s claim to joint family property warrants interference when the purchased property is the only joint family asset and no equities between the parties require adjustment.
material_facts: The appellant purchased the property from a member of a joint Hindu family.
The purchased property was the only joint family property available for partition.
The trial court, District Court and High Court had recorded concurrent findings.
issues.conclusion: The Court upheld the concurrent findings and dismissed the appeal without an order as to costs.
issues.legal_principle: A purchaser of joint family property from a family member may have a right to bring a general suit for partition, which may be the proper remedy. But where the purchased property is the only joint family property available for partition, there are no equities between the parties to adjust; the Court treated the question of the purchaser’s general partition remedy as academic in this case.

predicates.appeal_against_concurrent_findings: The purchaser appealed after multiple lower courts had recorded concurrent findings.
predicates.purchaser_bought_joint_family_property: A purchaser acquired joint family property from a member of the joint family.
predicates.property_is_only_joint_family_asset: The property acquired by the purchaser was the only joint family property available for partition.

issues.definition: When a purchaser appeals concurrent findings after acquiring joint family property that is the sole joint family asset, the appeal is dismissed.
